propertyTips.propertyTips.ap-long-text-indent: First-line indent for each paragraph of a long-text element, in characters: 2 means two Chinese characters wide (a common CJK convention), laid out in em units — it scales down when "Auto shrink" reduces the font size. Applies to long-text elements only; setting it on plain text has no effect.
propertyTips.propertyTips.ap-img-fit: How the image is scaled inside the element box. Contain: show the whole image, possibly with blank space. Crop: fill the box and take a region based on the crop anchor. Stretch: fill the box and distort. Original size / Shrink: never enlarge. The canvas and all three print pipelines use the same rule (Contain by default).
propertyTips.propertyTips.ap-img-object-position: Crop anchor (only shown for Crop mode): cropping scales the image to fill the box, and this picks which extra edge to keep. Choose a position preset (edge / center / opposite edge), then fine-tune with the percentage: 0 aligns left/top, 100 aligns to the other end; horizontal and vertical are independent. The default is centered (choose Top to keep the head in ID photos). Other fit modes have no crop edge, so this row is hidden.
propertyTips.propertyTips.ap-img-fit-scale: Crop zoom: after filling the box, enlarge the image by this much so both axes gain a crop margin — when image and box have the same aspect ratio, no zoom means nothing can be cropped. 100 = no zoom (default), maximum 400; anything outside the box is clipped by the element frame. The chosen anchor is both the pinning point and the zoom center. Shown for Crop mode only.
propertyTips.propertyTips.ap-rotate: Rotation of the element about its own center, in degrees (0–359). During printing, pagination and layout use the rotated bounding box: content that does not fit at the bottom moves to the next page, and content beyond the left/right/top paper edges is clipped with a print warning. Tables, flow lists and elements in the follow-up zone below a table do not support rotation (this row is hidden for them); arbitrary angles for barcodes and QR codes require a 385dpi+ print head — lower-resolution printers only output in 90° steps.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-columns: The number of cells per row must be specified by you — it is never inferred from content. If the column count times the cell width does not fit the element box, you get a hint but your value is not changed, and print output follows what you entered.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-row-height: Minimum height of each cell row, in millimetres, using the same rule as table row height: a row grows when its content is taller, and text is never clipped.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-gap-x: Horizontal whitespace between adjacent cells, in millimetres. No vertical gap is inserted; the distance between rows comes from the row height.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-auto-span: When a cell is wider than one column, let it span two or more columns; if the current row has too few columns left, move the whole cell to the start of the next row (never split a word). Off by default — when on, the printed column count depends on font size and box width.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-max-span: Upper limit for column spanning; it can never exceed "Columns per row". Lowering the column count also pushes this value down.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-layout-mode: What decides the container height. Fixed height: keep the designed height, one box per page, clip overflow (the default for existing templates, output unchanged). Dynamic pagination: the container grows with its content, continues row by row after a page fills, draws a complete border on every page, and follows the same rules as tables for the follow-up zone below the element.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-padding-top: Whitespace between the top of the container and the first content row in dynamic pagination mode, in millimetres. Only applies in dynamic mode; every page slice uses this padding and counts it in the pagination budget. Negative or invalid values are treated as 0.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-padding-right: Whitespace between the right side of the container and the content in dynamic pagination mode, in millimetres; it reduces the content width available for column-width estimation. Only applies in dynamic mode.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-padding-bottom: Whitespace between the bottom of the container and the last content row in dynamic pagination mode, in millimetres. Only applies in dynamic mode; every page slice uses this padding and counts it in the pagination budget.
propertyTips.propertyTips.fl-padding-left: Whitespace between the left side of the container and the content in dynamic pagination mode, in millimetres; it reduces the content width available for column-width estimation. Only applies in dynamic mode.
propertyTips.propertyTips.cd-bar-quiet-zone: Number of blank modules on each side of a barcode (1 module = 1 bar width): the default of 10 is the minimum required by 1D symbologies. Smaller values narrow the quiet zone and make bars thicker in the same box (they can be enlarged). Setting 0 removes the white margin, but the quiet zone participates in bar-space-bar transitions, so codes next to text or table lines may fail to scan — verify with a real print.
propertyTips.propertyTips.cd-bar-height: Target height of the black bars themselves, in millimetres (excluding the text below). The granularity is the physical width of one module, so only integer multiples are exact. Bar width takes priority: if the available height cannot fit the desired bar height, the height gives way — bars are never narrowed (thermal print clarity depends on bar width). This differs from "Maximum height", which limits the whole image including text.
propertyTips.propertyTips.cd-quiet-zone: Number of blank modules around a QR code: 0 means no white margin and the code scales to fill the element box (the surrounding white paper acts as the quiet zone). Larger values widen the margin and make the code smaller in the box. The default is 0; use 4 for the quiet zone recommended by ISO/IEC 18004.
